# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

1	# gba-emu build plan
2	
3	Goal: an original Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust, built as `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, exporting the 10
4	functions in `gba-eval/spec/ABI.md`, that scores above the 0.534 baseline on the gba-eval grader. The
5	grader's highest reachable score is 0.96, because the `comprehensive` subsystem carries weight but has no tests.
6	
7	Paths in this document are relative to this repo (`gba-trial/gba-emu`). The benchmark repo is
8	`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
9	
10	## Scope: must-have vs stretch
11	
12	| Phases | Status | Meaning |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
15	| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |
16	
17	A solid, verified 0-3 is worth more than a broken 0-6. Never start a stretch phase while a
18	must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower
19	than the last milestone.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)
24	
25	| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
28	| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
29	| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |
30	
31	Procedural subsystem weights: cpu 0.35, comprehensive 0.20 (no tests, always 0), memory 0.15,
32	timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.
33	
34	Consequences:
35	- **CPU correctness comes first.** Every other test depends on it.
36	- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.
37	- **Timing accuracy matters a lot**, because replay inputs land on fixed frame numbers. If the game boots
38	  a few frames later than in Mesen2, every button press lands at the wrong moment.
39	- **Colour precision is forgiving.** The grader quantises to 5 bits per channel, so any sensible
40	  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)
45	
46	Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
47	their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.
48	
49	One crate, `gba_emu`, with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`. The `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native
50	debug binary run on the host without wasm.
51	
52	```
53	src/
54	  lib.rs          ABI exports only (the 10 functions), thin wrappers over a single global Gba
55	  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
56	  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
57	  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
58	  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
59	  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
60	  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
61	  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation
62	  cpu/arm.rs      ARM (32-bit) decode + execute
63	  cpu/thumb.rs    THUMB (16-bit) decode + execute
64	  ppu/mod.rs      line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, line compositor, framebuffer
65	  ppu/bg_text.rs  tiled backgrounds (modes 0-2)
66	  ppu/bg_affine.rs rotation/scaling backgrounds
67	  ppu/bitmap.rs   modes 3/4/5
68	  ppu/obj.rs      sprites (normal + affine)
69	  ppu/effects.rs  windows, blending, mosaic
70	  timer.rs        4 timers, prescaler, cascade, overflow IRQ, FIFO tick
71	  dma.rs          4 DMA channels, triggers, priority
72	  apu/mod.rs      mixer, SOUNDCNT/SOUNDBIAS, output buffer, sample rate
73	  apu/psg.rs      channels 1-4
74	  apu/fifo.rs     direct sound channels A/B
75	  keypad.rs       KEYINPUT / KEYCNT
76	  cart.rs         ROM, save memory (SRAM / Flash / EEPROM), GPIO
77	src/bin/run_rom.rs  native debug tool: run a ROM for N frames, write the frame as .ppm and audio as .wav
78	```
79	
80	Contracts fixed in Phase 0:
81	
82	1. **Bus.** `fn read32(&mut self, addr: u32) -> u32` and the other widths, plus a cycle cost for each
83	   access. The CPU only talks to the bus, never to components directly.
84	2. **IO registers.** `io.rs` maps address ranges to owners: PPU `0x000-0x05F`, APU `0x060-0x0AF`,
85	   DMA `0x0B0-0x0DF`, timers `0x100-0x10F`, serial `0x120-0x12F` and `0x134-0x15F` (stub: plain storage, never
86	   connected), keypad `0x130-0x133`, IRQ/system `0x200-0x804`. Each owner
87	   exposes `io_read16(offset)` and `io_write16(offset, value)`, with 8- and 32-bit accesses split or
88	   merged centrally in `io.rs`. Each owner starts as a stub that its agent later fills in.
89	3. **Interrupts.** Any component calls `irq.request(IrqSource::VBlank)` etc. Only the CPU consumes interrupts.
90	4. **Timing.** `cpu.step()` returns the cycles it used. `Gba::run_frame()` loops until 280,896 cycles
91	   (228 lines x 1232 cycles) have elapsed, advancing PPU, timers, DMA and APU by the same cycles.
92	   Where exactly a frame ends (start of VBlank or not) must match Mesen2. Verify this in Phase 0 by
93	   comparing early frames with the reference.
94	5. **Events between components.** The PPU signals HBlank/VBlank to DMA. Timers signal FIFO ticks to the
95	   APU, and the APU signals FIFO-empty to DMA. These go through plain method calls in `gba.rs`, not
96	   through components holding references to each other.
97	6. **BIOS.** `gba-eval/spec/gba_bios_stub.bin` is embedded with `include_bytes!` and mapped at
98	   `0x00000000`. The CPU starts at the reset vector in ARM mode and runs it as normal code.
99	7. **ABI.** All 10 exports exist from day one. No imports: no `std::println!` in the wasm build,
100	   no threads, no allocation after init on hot paths. Do not export `emu_boot_frames`.
101	
102	Phase 0 deliverable: the ABI works end to end, the BIOS is mapped, and the CPU can be a stub.
103	`run_rom` writes a black frame. `scripts/grade-subset.sh ... smoke <any test>` runs without
104	"skip: trapped" (score ~0 is expected).

109	
110	Each phase lists its agents (run in parallel), the files they own, and the test that shows it worked.
111	"Gate" means the integrator merges the phase only when the gate passes.
112	
113	Smoke set (run on every merge, about 20 s):
114	`aw-arm-alu aw-thumb-alu memory timer-reload dma-priority tonc-snd1`

# gba-emu build plan

Goal: an original Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust, built as `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, exporting the 10
functions in `gba-eval/spec/ABI.md`, that scores above the 0.534 baseline on the gba-eval grader. The
grader's highest reachable score is 0.96, because the `comprehensive` subsystem carries weight but has no tests.

Paths in this document are relative to this repo (`gba-trial/gba-emu`). The benchmark repo is
`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.

## Scope: must-have vs stretch

| Phases | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |

A solid, verified 0-3 is worth more than a broken 0-6. Never start a stretch phase while a
must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower
than the last milestone.

---

## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)

| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |

Procedural subsystem weights: cpu 0.35, comprehensive 0.20 (no tests, always 0), memory 0.15,
timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.

Consequences:
- **CPU correctness comes first.** Every other test depends on it.
- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.
- **Timing accuracy matters a lot**, because replay inputs land on fixed frame numbers. If the game boots
  a few frames later than in Mesen2, every button press lands at the wrong moment.
- **Colour precision is forgiving.** The grader quantises to 5 bits per channel, so any sensible
  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.

---

## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)

Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.

One crate, `gba_emu`, with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`. The `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native
debug binary run on the host without wasm.

```
src/
  lib.rs          ABI exports only (the 10 functions), thin wrappers over a single global Gba
  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation
  cpu/arm.rs      ARM (32-bit) decode + execute
  cpu/thumb.rs    THUMB (16-bit) decode + execute
  ppu/mod.rs      line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, line compositor, framebuffer
  ppu/bg_text.rs  tiled backgrounds (modes 0-2)
  ppu/bg_affine.rs rotation/scaling backgrounds
  ppu/bitmap.rs   modes 3/4/5
  ppu/obj.rs      sprites (normal + affine)
  ppu/effects.rs  windows, blending, mosaic
  timer.rs        4 timers, prescaler, cascade, overflow IRQ, FIFO tick
  dma.rs          4 DMA channels, triggers, priority
  apu/mod.rs      mixer, SOUNDCNT/SOUNDBIAS, output buffer, sample rate
  apu/psg.rs      channels 1-4
  apu/fifo.rs     direct sound channels A/B
  keypad.rs       KEYINPUT / KEYCNT
  cart.rs         ROM, save memory (SRAM / Flash / EEPROM), GPIO
src/bin/run_rom.rs  native debug tool: run a ROM for N frames, write the frame as .ppm and audio as .wav
```

Contracts fixed in Phase 0:

1. **Bus.** `fn read32(&mut self, addr: u32) -> u32` and the other widths, plus a cycle cost for each
   access. The CPU only talks to the bus, never to components directly.
2. **IO registers.** `io.rs` maps address ranges to owners: PPU `0x000-0x05F`, APU `0x060-0x0AF`,
   DMA `0x0B0-0x0DF`, timers `0x100-0x10F`, serial `0x120-0x12F` and `0x134-0x15F` (stub: plain storage, never
   connected), keypad `0x130-0x133`, IRQ/system `0x200-0x804`. Each owner
   exposes `io_read16(offset)` and `io_write16(offset, value)`, with 8- and 32-bit accesses split or
   merged centrally in `io.rs`. Each owner starts as a stub that its agent later fills in.
3. **Interrupts.** Any component calls `irq.request(IrqSource::VBlank)` etc. Only the CPU consumes interrupts.
4. **Timing.** `cpu.step()` returns the cycles it used. `Gba::run_frame()` loops until 280,896 cycles
   (228 lines x 1232 cycles) have elapsed, advancing PPU, timers, DMA and APU by the same cycles.
   Where exactly a frame ends (start of VBlank or not) must match Mesen2. Verify this in Phase 0 by
   comparing early frames with the reference.
5. **Events between components.** The PPU signals HBlank/VBlank to DMA. Timers signal FIFO ticks to the
   APU, and the APU signals FIFO-empty to DMA. These go through plain method calls in `gba.rs`, not
   through components holding references to each other.
6. **BIOS.** `gba-eval/spec/gba_bios_stub.bin` is embedded with `include_bytes!` and mapped at

7. **ABI.** All 10 exports exist from day one. No imports: no `std::println!` in the wasm build,
   no threads, no allocation after init on hot paths. Do not export `emu_boot_frames`.

2

4	functions in `gba-eval/spec/ABI.md`, that scores above the 0.534 baseline on the gba-eval grader. The
5	grader's highest reachable score is 0.96, because the `comprehensive` subsystem carries weight but has no tests.
6	
7	Paths in this document are relative to this repo (`gba-trial/gba-emu`). The benchmark repo is
8	`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
9	
10	## Scope: must-have vs stretch
11	
12	| Phases | Status | Meaning |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
15	| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |
16	
17	A solid, verified 0-3 is worth more than a broken 0-6. Never start a stretch phase while a
18	must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower
19	than the last milestone.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)
24	
25	| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
28	| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
29	| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |
30

32	timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.
33	
34	Consequences:
35	- **CPU correctness comes first.** Every other test depends on it.
36	- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.
37	- **Timing accuracy matters a lot**, because replay inputs land on fixed frame numbers. If the game boots
38	  a few frames later than in Mesen2, every button press lands at the wrong moment.
39	- **Colour precision is forgiving.** The grader quantises to 5 bits per channel, so any sensible
40	  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.

44	## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)
45	
46	Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
47	their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.

53	src/
54	  lib.rs          ABI exports only (the 10 functions), thin wrappers over a single global Gba
55	  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
56	  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
57	  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
58	  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
59	  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
60	  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
61	  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation

80	Contracts fixed in Phase 0:
81	
82	1. **Bus.** `fn read32(&mut self, addr: u32) -> u32` and the other widths, plus a cycle cost for each
83	   access. The CPU only talks to the bus, never to components directly.
84	2. **IO registers.** `io.rs` maps address ranges to owners: PPU `0x000-0x05F`, APU `0x060-0x0AF`,
85	   DMA `0x0B0-0x0DF`, timers `0x100-0x10F`, serial `0x120-0x12F` and `0x134-0x15F` (stub: plain storage, never
86	   connected), keypad `0x130-0x133`, IRQ/system `0x200-0x804`. Each owner
87	   exposes `io_read16(offset)` and `io_write16(offset, value)`, with 8- and 32-bit accesses split or

96	   through components holding references to each other.

100	   no threads, no allocation after init on hot paths. Do not export `emu_boot_frames`.

content.text:
I found no correctness problems, so this can merge. Every finding below is minor.

**Did the deferral move anything?** I traced each path the task named and none of them moves.

- **When the deferral ends:** the deferred cycles are only applied once they reach the earliest upcoming event. That catch-up happens at the end of the same step where the old code would have handled the event, so IRQs are raised and DMA requests (HBlank, VBlank, FIFO) are flagged at the same step boundary as before.
- **IO reads and writes:** every IO access first brings PPU, timers and APU up to the end of the previous step, which is the same state the old code had at that point. Because the deferred cycles are always below the next event, an IO catch-up never fires an event early. Any IO write forces a fresh event calculation at the end of the step.
- **Timer reads:** the existing within-instruction timer catch-up still uses the cycles from the same reference point. The overflow estimate `start_delay + (ticks << shift) - prescaler_cycles + cycles_already_run` matches how `ticks_from_cycles` and `step` count. Timers chained to the one below ("count-up" timers) are correctly skipped, because they only overflow when that lower timer does.
- **FIFO pops and audio samples:** within one catch-up the order stays timers first, then the APU. The sound-channel stepping I checked (`advance_timer`, the frame-sequencer split) gives the same result whether it runs in one chunk or many. The point where a sample is mixed is computed exactly from the accumulated cycles.
- **Halt:** `halted_cycles` adding `deferred_component_cycles` stays below the next boundary, because the deferred cycles never reach a PPU line event.
- **Frame end:** the frame ends with a full catch-up.
- **Memory reads:** the `read_le16`/`read_le32` change behaves the same way.

**Empirical check.** I built `run_rom` at the merge base (78c6836) and on the branch. I ran 600 frames of all 16 homebrew ROMs and the first 60 test ROMs. All 76 gave byte-identical `.ppm` and `.wav` output. These runs had no button input, so the input paths are covered by your new reset test rather than by this check.

**Other checks**
- **Tests and builds:** `cargo test` (129 passed, debug and release) and the wasm build both pass. The new test `tests::reset_reproduces_load_rom_exactly` really runs and passes, rather than skipping.
- **Ownership:** all changes are inside the files the worker was allowed to touch. `scheduler.rs`, `irq.rs`, `dma.rs` and `Cargo.toml` are unchanged.
- **Hacks and originality:** nothing branches on a specific ROM, and I saw nothing that looks taken from another emulator. The only magic numbers are the standard FNV-1a hash constants, and the doc comment names them.

**Findings** (paths are in the branch worktree `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae4071a9857319cb4`)
- `src/apu/mod.rs:72`: [minor] The new method `cycles_until_sample()` returns the opposite of the existing field `cycles_until_sample` (line 46), which actually counts cycles since the last sample. Rename the field to `cycles_since_sample`.
- `src/timer.rs:179`, `src/ppu/mod.rs:220`, `src/apu/mod.rs:72`: [minor] The three "cycles until next event" functions carry the whole no-behaviour-change guarantee but have no unit tests. Suggested fix: one test each asserting that stepping `n - 1` cycles fires no event and stepping `n` does (timer overflow with a prescaler and start delay, HBlank, sample).
- `src/bus.rs:252`: [minor] `Bus::catch_up_components` calls `crate::gba::advance_components`, so `bus` now depends on `gba`. That inverts the layering in PLAN.md and moves part of the main loop into `bus.rs`. Acceptable, but note it in NOTES.md as a contract change.
- `src/bus.rs:216-219`: [minor] `deferred_component_cycles` and `cycles_until_component_event` are `pub` and can be changed from anywhere, while correctness depends on keeping deferred cycles below the next event. Make them `pub(crate)`.
- `src/lib.rs:166`: [minor] The determinism test hard-codes an absolute path to a corpus ROM and silently passes if the file is missing. Accept that as documented, or make the skip more visible.

I removed the scratch worktree I used for the merge-base build.
